lines.text: Who are you using as your measuring stick?
Job applicants rated their self-esteem while another candidate waited in the room.
Sometimes he was polished and sharp. Sometimes, messy and unprepared.
Next to the polished rival, their self-esteem dropped.
Next to the sloppy one, it rose.
Same person. Same skills. Only the comparison changed.
So choose your measuring stick on purpose.

post.title: Why You Feel Worse Next to Certain People #shorts
post.description: Your self-esteem depends on who's in the room. In Morse & Gergen (1970), job applicants' self-esteem dropped when a polished, well-prepared rival sat nearby and rose next to a sloppy one. That's social comparison. #psychology #selfesteem #confidence
